papers_read.title_as_printed: Development of a Machine Learning Model to Discriminate Mild Cognitive Impairment Subjects from Normal Controls in Community Screening (Jiang, Zhang, Li, Yu, Yan, Jiang; Brain Sci. 2022, 12, 1149)
Mild Cognitive Impairment detection based on EEG and HRV data (Boudaya, Chaabene, Bouaziz, Hoekelmann, Chaari; Digital Signal Processing 147 (2024) 104399)

what_each_reports.P-214: Shanghai community screening. Cohort 1 (336 subjects, training/validation) and independent Cohort 2 (44 MCI / 48 NC). Features: single-electrode wearable EEG, eye tracking, a 20-subtest neuropsychological battery, plus demographics; MRMR selection, RBF-SVM. Subject-level MCI vs NC: Cohort 1 5-fold CV accuracy 84.5 +/- 4.43%, AUC 0.94; independent Cohort 2 accuracy 88.8 +/- 3.59%, AUC 0.966. MCI itself is defined by neuropsychological performance (Jak/Bondi actuarial criteria).
what_each_reports.P-83: Magdeburg; 15 participants (8 MCI, 7 HC) after excluding 9 of 24. 14-channel Emotiv EEG and Polar H10 HRV recorded during CERAD subtests; features from 3-second windows; 75/25 shuffled split of segments; SVM/GB/RF hard-voting hybrid. Mean accuracy across seven CERAD subtests 93.86% (range 86.19-97.43%; best T1 verbal fluency 97.43%, AUC 94.91%). 10-fold and LOOCV over 100 runs: 86.03-95.23% / 86.02-96.14%. Re-implementing P-214's method (Jiang et al. [93]) on its own data gave a mean of 87.68%.

quantity_a: Subject-level accuracy of MCI vs normal controls in community screening, EEG (1 electrode) + eye tracking + neuropsychological battery, 5-fold CV in Cohort 1 (84.5%) with an independent test cohort (88.8%).
quantity_b: Segment-level accuracy (3-second EEG/HRV windows, shuffled 75/25 split, so windows from the same 15 people fall in both training and test sets) of MCI vs healthy control, averaged over seven CERAD subtests (93.86%).
incompatible_if_same: No. Two different feature sets and classifiers on two different cohorts each report their own accuracy. P-83 does rank its method above P-214's, but on P-83's own 15-person data, where the P-214 pipeline scored 87.68%, close to P-214's own 84.5-88.8%; P-214 never tests P-83's method, so no ordering is refuted.

gates.task: match: both MCI vs cognitively normal detection (T1)
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: two distinct private cohorts (Shanghai Jiading/Baoshan communities vs a Magdeburg clinical study); the record's dataset_equal 'Yes' rests on both registry rows reading 'not reported'
gates.validation_tier: mismatch in substance: P-214 has subject-level CV plus an independent external cohort; P-83 has a segment-level random split and CV within 15 subjects with no external cohort
gates.modality_family: partial match: both use EEG, but P-214 adds eye tracking and a neuropsychological battery, and P-83 adds HRV recorded during a cognitive task

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both say 'accuracy', but P-214 classifies people while P-83 classifies 3-second signal windows (with subject overlap between training and test), so the two accuracies are for different units of analysis; predictor sets also differ.
performance_validity: P-83's headline 93.86% is below 0.97, so the automatic flag is not tripped (pack: performance_suspect false). But the paper's best per-test figure is 97.43% (T1), from internal validation of 15 participants with no external cohort, which meets the Section 2 criterion; the 93.86% average rests on the same segment-level split. So a performance comparison resting on P-83 could not be genuine even if the quantities matched.
independence: Distinct author groups and cohorts; P-83 cites P-214 as reference [93] and re-implements its method on P-83's data.
grounds: P-214 reports subject-level accuracy with an independent test cohort, whereas P-83 reports accuracy over 3-second windows split at random, so windows from the same 15 people are in both training and test sets; the two accuracies measure different things.

The predictor sets differ: P-214 includes a neuropsychological battery (the same kind of testing that defines its MCI label) with EEG and eye tracking, while P-83 uses EEG and HRV recorded during CERAD.
The dataset-family gate fails (two unrelated private cohorts) and no waiver is on record.

Even setting this aside, P-83's own re-run of P-214's pipeline (87.68%) agrees with P-214's reported accuracy, so there is no disagreement, and P-83's best figure (97.43%, n=15, internal only) meets the performance-validity exclusion.

evidence_quotes.quote: We found that the classification accuracy of the proposed model achieved 84.5 +/- 4.43% and 88.8 +/- 3.59% in Cohort 1 and Cohort 2, respectively.
Cohort 2 was used as an independent test group to verify the robustness of the classification results.
Our dataset includes 15 subjects who were randomly assigned to training and testing groups of 7 HC and 8 MCI, respectively.
For each test, we separated our data into 75% for the training set and 25% for the testing set. ... we applied the shuffling strategy throughout the data partitioning process.

Notably, an impressive enhancement in average accuracy of all tests, reaching 93.86%, is observed. ... the first test called 'Verbal fluency' related to the executive function had the highest accuracy (97.43%).

record_defects: resolution_note's ground 'Same architecture family (A4_transformer)' is false: neither paper uses a transformer (P-214 RBF-SVM; P-83 SVM/GB/RF voting ensemble).
dataset_equal 'Yes' is wrong: the cohorts are unrelated (Shanghai communities vs Magdeburg).
claim_b's 93.86% is a segment-level average over seven CERAD subtests from 15 participants, not a subject-level accuracy.

Registry Sample_N_Approx for P-214 is 428 (336 + 92), consistent with the paper; P-214's own text swaps the Cohort 1 group sizes (abstract '184 MCI patients and 152 NC'; Table 1 and Section 3.1 '152 MCI ... 184 NC').
resolution says 'Rejected - false positive' while resolution_status is partially_resolved_candidate: internally inconsistent.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A subject-level, externally validated P-83 result on a matched feature set that fell outside P-214's reported uncertainty; the paper has no such analysis.
